blocks.h2: When Your Faucet Needs Repair or Replacement
blocks.intro: Most faucet problems start small. Here's when to call:

tiles.body: A worn cartridge, washer or seal is the usual cause. A steady drip wastes more water than most people think.
If one faucet is weak and the rest are fine, the aerator or cartridge may be clogged. If every faucet is weak, it may be the pipes.
Water in the cabinet usually comes from a supply line, a shutoff valve or the faucet base. Catch it before it damages the cabinet.

tiles.h3: Hard to Turn or Loose Handles
tiles.body: Stiff, wobbly or grinding handles mean worn internal parts. Sometimes a repair, sometimes it's time for a new faucet.

bodies: The kitchen faucet gets more use than any other fixture in the house. We repair drips, leaks, weak spray and loose handles, and we install new kitchen faucets, including pull-down and pull-out models, faucets with side sprayers and filtered water taps.

A new faucet is also a good time to replace the shutoff valves and supply lines under the sink. In older homes, those valves may not have been turned in years, and they're often the part that fails. We'll check them and tell you if they need replacing.

Beyond the faucet, we handle the rest of the plumbing in your kitchen: sink drains and traps, dishwasher hookups, ice maker lines, garbage disposals and gas lines for ranges. For a remodel, we can move or add fixtures so the plumbing matches your new layout.

If your kitchen sink is clogged, see [drain cleaning](/highland-park/drain-cleaning). For disposal problems, see [garbage disposal repair](/highland-park/garbage-disposal-installation-repair). For a new gas range, see [gas line installation](/highland-park/gas-line-installation).

img.alt: Plumbing under a double kitchen sink: white PVC drain and P-trap, braided supply lines with chrome shutoff valves, and a garbage disposal

bodies: We install sinks, faucets, toilets, showerheads, tub spouts, laundry sinks and outdoor spigots, whether you're replacing one fixture or doing a full remodel. Every install includes the connections, shutoff valves and a leak check before we leave.

Buying your own fixtures? That's fine. Tell us the make and model when you call and we'll let you know if anything about your plumbing needs to change to fit it. For toilets, see [toilet installation](/highland-park/toilet-installation-repair). For showers, see [shower repair](/highland-park/shower-repair).

blocks.h2: Faucets and Fixtures in Older Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960. Older plumbing behind a new faucet can be the difference between a quick swap and a surprise.

items.body: Shutoff valves that haven't been turned in decades can seize or start leaking the moment they're used. We check them first and replace them if they won't hold.
Older galvanized water lines can narrow with corrosion, which shows up as low pressure at new faucets. We'll tell you if the fixture or the pipe is the problem.

blocks.h2: What Happens When You Call J. Blanton
blocks.intro: A faucet job should be simple. Here's how we keep it that way.

steps.body: Your plumber explains what's wrong in plain English first, then walks you through your options. You decide.

steps.h3: 2. A Clear Price Before Any Work Starts
steps.body: You get a flat-rate price before we touch anything, with no surprise add-ons when the job is done.
Shoe covers on, work area protected, and the space cleaned up before we leave.

blocks.h2: Faucet and Fixture Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: Should I repair or replace my faucet?
items.preview: A worn part on a good faucet is a repair. An old or corroded faucet is usually a replacement.
items.answer: If it's a worn cartridge, washer or seal on a good-quality faucet, a repair usually makes sense. If the faucet is old, corroded or parts are hard to find, replacing it is often the better value. We'll tell you which one we'd pick.

items.q: Can I buy my own faucet and have you install it?
items.preview: Yes. Tell us the make and model and we'll confirm it fits.
items.answer: Yes. Tell us the make and model when you call. We'll check that it fits your sink and plumbing and let you know if anything needs to change.

items.q: Why is my new faucet's water pressure low?
items.preview: Check the aerator first. If every faucet is low, it may be older pipes.
items.answer: Check the aerator first, since debris often gets trapped there after install. If pressure is low at every faucet, older galvanized pipes narrowed by corrosion may be the cause.

items.q: How much does faucet installation cost?
items.preview: It depends on the faucet and your plumbing. You get a flat price before any work begins.
items.answer: It depends on the faucet, the sink, the condition of the shutoff valves and supply lines, and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
